title: Directories disappear in Filer Store
body:
Sponsors SeaweedFS via Patreon https://www.patreon.com/seaweedfs

**Describe the bug**
We encountered weird issue with missing directories in Filer Store. For instance, we have directory `/buckets/mybucket/dir1/dir2/dir3`, some files in `dir3` and some job that writes new files, removes old files, etc. Sometimes we observe situation when intermediate folders (dir3, or dir2, etc) got missing. From Filer Store perspective it should look like this:
| directory                        | name      | metadata |
|----------------------------------|-----------|----------|
| /buckets/mybucket/dir1           | dir2      | ...      |
| /buckets/mybucket/dir1/dir2      | dir3      | ...      |
| /buckets/mybucket/dir1/dir2      | dir31      | ...      |
| /buckets/mybucket/dir1/dir2      | dir32      | ...      |
| /buckets/mybucket/dir1/dir2/dir3 | file1.txt | ...      |
| /buckets/mybucket/dir1/dir2/dir3 | file2.txt | ...      |

But sometimes we see it like this:
| directory                        | name      | metadata |
|----------------------------------|-----------|----------|
| /buckets/mybucket/dir1           | dir2      | ...      |
| /buckets/mybucket/dir1/dir2      | dir31      | ...      |
| /buckets/mybucket/dir1/dir2      | dir32      | ...      |
| /buckets/mybucket/dir1/dir2/dir3 | file1.txt | ...      |
| /buckets/mybucket/dir1/dir2/dir3 | file2.txt | ...      |

As you can see, entry with directory=/buckets/mybucket/dir1/dir2 and name=dir3 is missing. Because of this, in Filer UI we cannot see dir3 when listing dir2 and thus cannot list dir3 (technically, we can if we know dir3 exists, but if we don't - we can't list it).

For quite long time we have tried to catch it in the logs of the Filer and recently we finally did it. It looks like this:
```
filer-1 | I1004 08:25:00.054881 filer_server_handlers_write_autochunk.go:202 saving /buckets/spark/checkpoint/foo/s-3/bar/events/s3/bar/offsets/.18.c18d2228-b40d-411c-a7a6-5eb71f5a9455.tmp
filer-1 | I1004 08:25:00.055701 filer.go:264 find uncached directory: /buckets/spark/checkpoint/foo/s-3/bar/events/s3/bar/offsets
filer-1 | I1004 08:25:00.056928 filer.go:228 InsertEntry /buckets/spark/checkpoint/foo/s-3/bar/events/s3/bar/offsets/.18.c18d2228-b40d-411c-a7a6-5eb71f5a9455.tmp: new entry: .18.c18d2228-b40d-411c-a7a6-5eb71f5a9455.tmp
filer-1 | I1004 08:25:00.060795 filer.go:249 CreateEntry /buckets/spark/checkpoint/foo/s-3/bar/events/s3/bar/offsets/.18.c18d2228-b40d-411c-a7a6-5eb71f5a9455.tmp: created
...
filer-2 | I1004 08:25:00.140618 filer_server_handlers_write_autochunk.go:202 saving /buckets/spark/checkpoint/foo/s-3/bar/events/s3/bar/offsets/18
filer-2 | I1004 08:25:00.141376 filer.go:264 find uncached directory: /buckets/spark/checkpoint/foo/s-3/bar/events/s3/bar/offsets
filer-2 | I1004 08:25:00.143137 filer.go:228 InsertEntry /buckets/spark/checkpoint/foo/s-3/bar/events/s3/bar/offsets/18: new entry: 18
filer-2 | I1004 08:25:00.146240 filer.go:249 CreateEntry /buckets/spark/checkpoint/foo/s-3/bar/events/s3/bar/offsets/18: created
filer-3 | I1004 08:25:00.146616 filer_grpc_server.go:24 LookupDirectoryEntry /buckets/spark/checkpoint/foo/s-3/bar/events/s3/bar/offsets/18
filer-3 | I1004 08:25:00.151830 filer_grpc_server.go:24 LookupDirectoryEntry /buckets/spark/checkpoint/foo/s-3/bar/events/s3/bar/offsets/.18.c18d2228-b40d-411c-a7a6-5eb71f5a9455.tmp
filer-3 | I1004 08:25:00.152787 filer_grpc_server.go:292 DeleteEntry name:"/buckets/spark/checkpoint/foo/s-3/bar/events/s3/bar/offsets/.18.c18d2228-b40d-411c-a7a6-5eb71f5a9455.tmp"  is_delete_data:true
filer-3 | I1004 08:25:00.154329 filer_delete_entry.go:124 deleting entry /buckets/spark/checkpoint/foo/s-3/bar/events/s3/bar/offsets/.18.c18d2228-b40d-411c-a7a6-5eb71f5a9455.tmp, delete chunks: true
filer-3 | I1004 08:25:00.155963 filer_grpc_server.go:292 DeleteEntry name:"/buckets/spark/checkpoint/foo/s-3/bar/events/s3/bar/offsets"
filer-3 | I1004 08:25:00.159436 filer_delete_entry.go:110 deleting directory /buckets/spark/checkpoint/foo/s-3/bar/events/s3/bar/offsets delete chunks: false
filer-3 | I1004 08:25:00.160952 filer_delete_entry.go:124 deleting entry /buckets/spark/checkpoint/foo/s-3/bar/events/s3/bar/offsets, delete chunks: false
```

So, the sequence:
- S3 saved `.18.c18d2228-b40d-411c-a7a6-5eb71f5a9455.tmp` into the directory
- S3 saved `18` into the directoru
- S3 removed `.18.c18d2228-b40d-411c-a7a6-5eb71f5a9455.tmp` from the directory
- S3 tried to remove directory ([here](https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweedfs/blob/35fd1e1c9af62df7ca50324a0db2983ac4af4176/weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_delete.go#L162), I suppose ). Directory should not remove as it is not empty, but for some reason listing ([here](https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweedfs/blob/35fd1e1c9af62df7ca50324a0db2983ac4af4176/weed/filer/filer_delete_entry.go#L75), I suppose) did not return any entries from directory as well as any errors of listing itself, and the directory got deleted.

Issue reproduces occasionally, I didn't find any way to force to reproduce it yet.

**System Setup**
We have SeaweedFS running on Kubernetes via SeaweedFS Operator. There are 3 Masters, 16 Volume Servers, 4 Filers (with ScyllaDB as its backend)

List the command line to start "weed master", "weed volume", "weed filer", "weed s3", "weed mount":
Master:
```
weed -logtostderr=true master -volumeSizeLimitMB=30720 -defaultReplication=001 -ip=$(POD_NAME).seaweedfs1-master-peer.seaweedfs -peers=seaweedfs1-master-0.seaweedfs1-master-peer.seaweedfs:9333,seaweedfs1-master-1.seaweedfs1-master-peer.seaweedfs:9333,seaweedfs1-master-2.seaweedfs1-master-peer.seaweedfs:9333 -metricsPort=9999
```
Volume Server:
```
weed -logtostderr=true volume -port=8444 -max=0 -ip=$(POD_NAME).seaweedfs1-volume-peer.seaweedfs -metricsPort=9999 -mserver=seaweedfs1-master-0.seaweedfs1-master-peer.seaweedfs:9333,seaweedfs1-master-1.seaweedfs1-master-peer.seaweedfs:9333,seaweedfs1-master-2.seaweedfs1-master-peer.seaweedfs:9333 -dir=/data0 -concurrentDownloadLimitMB=0 -concurrentUploadLimitMB=0
```
Filer:
```
weed -logtostderr=true filer -port=8888 -ip=$(POD_NAME).seaweedfs1-filer-peer.seaweedfs -master=seaweedfs1-master-0.seaweedfs1-master-peer.seaweedfs:9333,seaweedfs1-master-1.seaweedfs1-master-peer.seaweedfs:9333,seaweedfs1-master-2.seaweedfs1-master-peer.seaweedfs:9333 -metricsPort=9999 -s3 -concurrentUploadLimitMB=0
```
OS version: `Fedora CoreOS 33.20210426.3.0`
output of weed version: `version 8000GB 3.59 27b34f379 linux amd64`
if using filer, show the content of filer.toml:
```
[leveldb2]
enabled = false
[etcd]
enabled = false
servers = "seaweed-etcd.seaweedfs:2379"
timeout = "3s"
[cassandra]
enabled = true
keyspace="seaweedfs"
hosts=[
  "seaweed-scylla-client.seaweedfs:9042",
]
superLargeDirectories = [
]
```

We've also tried to rebuild SeaweedFS binary with `go mod edit -replace github.com/gocql/gocql=github.com/scylladb/gocql@v${SCYLLA_DRIVER_VER}` in order to check if the issue in Cassandra driver, but no luck - issure reproduces with ScyllaDB driver as well.

**Expected behavior**
Directory should not be deleted if it is not empty and DeleteEntry call has isRecursive=false
